utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: Yes, there were such men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: For clarification, does -- does that question go to the column or the group of people this witness was with, or does it go clear back to the column that left towards Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. You can deal with this yourself, Mr. Thayer. Thank you, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Witness, with respect to the civilians with whom you were walking in this column, from the time you left Srebrenica to the time you were captured, were there individuals whom you have never seen nor heard from again that you knew personally?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: Yes, of course there are such individuals.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Sir, you mentioned that you had been living with your father in Srebrenica at the time of the attack.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Would you please describe for the Trial Chamber the last time you had an opportunity to see him?

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: (redacted)On the 11th of July, I went to the place where I resided. I met up with him. I tried to comfort him. I tried telling him that the situation would turn for the better and that the events, the previous events, would not repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, before I ask my last question, I think we need a redaction at page 61, lines 5 through 6.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Even line 4. I would -- I would play it safe. Lines 4 to 6, up to the word -- in line 6, the end of that sentence. Up to the full stop before the words "on the 11th of July." Thank you. I was going to point that out myself, actually. We are in open session, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Witness, have you ever seen or heard from your father since that conversation that you described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: With respect to the men with whom you were captured, who you identified previously, have you ever seen or heard from those individuals?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. THAYER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. That concludes my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thayer. I think what I'm suggesting, in agreement with the Judges, is that we have the break now. It has to be a 30-minute break in any case. And then we will have just under an hour for the first cross-examinations, which will, of course, be all conducted with the caveat that we pointed out earlier. We're having the break now so that you discuss amongst yourselves who goes first, because one may have -- be in a better position than another to cover some territory today. Thank you. Thirty minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Who is requesting first? Mr. Meek. Thank you, Mr. Meek. And when you think you've covered what you could, what you can cover today, you can stop, and the understanding is you can continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the same applies to anyone else who is second or third. Mr. Meek. Mr. Meek is representing Colonel Beara in this case, and he will be starting his cross-examination today and continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness. How are you today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Very well, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Witness, can I take it that you never gave a statement to any person, organisation, or entity until the 2nd day of May, 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Then can you please tell me how many statements you have given prior to your giving a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor here in The Hague on the 2nd day of May of 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: I have not provided any statements to anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And, Witness, can you tell me, please, and tell the Judges what was your -- what were your inducements to give this statement and come here to testify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: Because I went through all this, and I wanted this truth to surface one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And can you tell me, please, why it is that it took 11 years for this truth, as you say, to surface?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: I don't know. You should ask somebody else that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And who would you propose that I ask that question to, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't give you an answer to that question. I can't tell you who you should ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Do you recall the date that you were released from the Batkovici camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Approximately what day and month and year was that, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: I believe that it was on the 26th of December, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And when you were released, where did you go immediately, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: Buses came and there was an exchange at Sockovacki bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And then my question, sir, is where did the bus take you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: To the place of exchange that I have just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: All right. Let me -- that's my fault. After you were exchanged, after the exchange, where did you end up initially?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: We were transferred to Tuzla on board another bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And after your arrival in Tuzla, is it your testimony, under oath, that nobody everybody asked you what happened to you and that you never gave any statements to the authorities in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: There were some questions, but they were very short. I have never provided any detailed information about my ordeal to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can you tell me, when these questions were asked, did the person or persons who were questioning you, did they have a tape recorder? Did they take notes? And, in fact, were you ever shown a written statement that was drafted from the questions that you were asked in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: I don't know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Now, you said state earlier that you had never provided any detailed information about your ordeal to anybody before the 2nd day of May of 2006; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: And how did you get ahold of the Office of the Prosecutor to volunteer your services as a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: Yes, they did get my information, and they got in touch with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Can you tell me what information they obtained, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-106
utterances.text: They got information that I was a Srebrenica tragedy survivor and that I was in the Batkovic camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, we might want to go into private session out of caution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
